name: Iceland
policy_rate_title: Central Bank of Iceland key rate
policy_rate_name: Central Bank of Iceland key rate

notes.inflation: Inflation is Statistics Iceland's national consumer price index, which includes owner-occupied housing, not the EU's harmonised index: the change in the all-items index on twelve months, and on the previous month. The interest rate is the Central Bank of Iceland's key rate, the rate on seven-day term deposits, shown from June 2014, when it took its current form.
notes.labour: GDP and unemployment are Statistics Iceland's figures as the OECD republishes them. GDP is quarterly and seasonally adjusted, with real GDP in chain-linked volumes. Unemployment is monthly, from the labour force survey, seasonally adjusted, for people aged 15 and over.
notes.trade: Goods trade is Iceland's monthly data as the IMF republishes it, in US dollars, converted to krónur at each month's average exchange rate from the Bank for International Settlements. Exports are valued free on board, imports including cost, insurance and freight.
notes.public: Debt and the budget balance are the IMF World Economic Outlook's general government figures, actual years only, so estimates and projections never appear as data.
notes.markets: The exchange rate is the World Bank's annual average official rate, shown from 1981, when the new króna replaced the old at 100 to 1; the World Bank restates earlier years in new krónur. There is no 10-year government bond yield: the OECD's series for Iceland ended in August 2022. The OECD publishes no business confidence index for Iceland.
